newsitem.title: UK: Citibank executive sees US assets performing well.
newsitem.headline: Citibank executive sees US assets performing well.

text.p: Onno Ruding, vice chairman at Citibank, said on Monday U.S. assets were likely to continue to perform well, especially compared with European markets.

"The sentiment here in Switzerland is I think quite positive about the U.S. economy, about corporate America, and also about the dollar," said Ruding, speaking from the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
Ruding said U.S. markets looked good even though the dollar had risen against European currencies. "All the rigidities in Europe still hamper European economies, particularly Germany."

Compared to Japan, however, he said the dollar had less scope for gains. "The dollar has gone up so much already that I don't know whether there's much more room to improve further vis a vis the yen," Ruding said.
He said the most important thing in Europe was to reduce labour rigidities and he also thought it would be a good idea for further interest rate falls across Europe.

"I personally think the central banks in Europe should reduce somewhat further their discount rates because there is low inflation here in Europe, and the economic growth is rather low and unemployment is high."
Ruding said it would be detrimental if U.S. interest rates were to rise.
"I do not expect an increase in interest rates and I think it's unnecessary," he said. "There is no reason with this very low inflation rate."
